heard: Saturn's rings are wider than 20 Earths, but razor-thin. They span 170,000 miles, while averaging just 30 feet thick. This disk is like a city-sized circle thinner than cardboard. Galileo first saw them in 1610 and thought they were ears. Two years later, they vanished because Earth passed through their plane. Christian Huygens finally revealed their true shape as detached rings in 1659. These massive bands are actually 99.9% pure water ice. They are likely temporary, appearing only a hundred million years ago. Nothing in the solar system matches this massive scale.
